text: Defeating Mergo's Wet Nurse and approaching the crib causes Mergo's crying to stop, beginning the unraveling of the Mensis ritual's nightmare.
After the player kills the Orphan of Kos, the doll states that Gehrman is sleeping soundly for the first time in a long while.

Gehrman offers to use the Burial Blade to end the player's dream and grant them the same mercy he has given hundreds of hunters before; choosing to accept death at his hands offers a more melancholy, contemplative ending distinct from the combat-focused alternatives.
If the player has consumed enough umbilical cord fragments to resist its call, the Moon Presence descends and a final battle begins against it directly.
Defeating the Moon Presence leads to the Childhood's Beginning ending, where the player becomes an infant great one held by the doll.

Bloodborne's hidden true ending requires players to collect and correctly consume a specific number of Umbilical Cord items at the right moment; it was deliberately designed as an obscure secret to encourage community collaboration, and the community took time to fully document the requirement.
Bloodborne features three distinct possible endings tied to Gehrman, the Moon Presence, and the true nature of the Hunter's Dream.
The writers behind Bloodborne's endings deliberately avoided making any single ending clearly superior, wanting players to feel the weight of choice.
The most common ending for first-time players involves defeating the Moon Presence and inheriting its cosmic role, often reached without players realizing alternate endings exist.
Each of Bloodborne's three endings has a distinct final cutscene and musical cue.
The coronation-style visual language in some Bloodborne endings reflects a broader stylistic tendency shared with Elden Ring's similarly structured conclusions.
Reaching any of Bloodborne's endings does not require completing all available content, leaving much of the game's lore optional.
Bloodborne's ending sequences are visually and narratively restrained, avoiding extended aftermath or explicit consequence, consistent with the game's broader style of implication.
The game offers multiple distinct endings, reinforcing the theme that no single definitive answer resolves its questions about cosmic ambition and human limitation.
The game's ending sequences remain entirely wordless from the hunter's perspective, consistent with the silent protagonist approach.
Bloodborne's final piece of text encountered by most players, regardless of which ending they reach, is deliberately brief and understated, offering closure without fully resolving every question.
